messages:
Emma Liu: quick kickoff — I'm consolidating a small library of internal incident comms templates (status page blips, customer emails, internal Slack updates, and on-call handoffs). Want minimal, customer-first phrasing + clear placeholders. Posting a first draft below, please comment inline or add alternatives.

Raj Patel: this is awesome, thanks. Couple high-level principles i want to keep upfront: 1) short headline + one-line impact, 2) what we're doing now (action), 3) what customers can expect next / ETA if we have one, 4) links/contacts for follow-up. Avoid technical conjecture in public updates.

Sasha Kim: +1 to Raj. Also: prefer active voice not passive. e.g., "We are investigating" not "an investigation is underway".

incident-bot: New incident created INC-2026-045 by PagerDuty at 2026-03-15T14:12:01Z

Emma Liu: Draft 1 — status page snippets (short, single-line headline + body). Please pick the tone you think should be canonical for public vs internal.

-- STATUS PAGE: INVESTIGATING (public) --
Headline: "Investigating increased API error rate"
Body: "We are currently investigating an increase in 5xx errors for the Redwood API that may affect some customers. Our engineers are actively investigating. We will post updates here as we learn more. No customer data loss has been detected at this time."

-- STATUS PAGE: MITIGATING (public) --
Headline: "Mitigation in progress — partial recovery"
Body: "We have identified a mitigation and are rolling it out. Some customers may see improved success rates; others may still be impacted. We continue to monitor and will provide an update when the issue is fully resolved."

-- STATUS PAGE: RESOLVED (public) --
Headline: "Incident resolved — service restored"
Body: "The issue that caused increased API error rates has been resolved. Customers should see normal operation. We will follow up with a post-incident summary with root cause and long-term fixes."

Raj Patel: I like those. Two micro-edits: 1) swap "No customer data loss has been detected" to "We have no evidence of customer data loss at this time" (less absolute), 2) add a standard line for customers wanting support: "If you continue to experience issues, contact support@redwood.ai or open a support ticket."

Emma Liu: noted, will incorporate.

-- CUSTOMER EMAIL TEMPLATE (short alert) --
Subject: "Redwood — Service update: {{short_headline}} ({{incident_id}})"
Body:
Hi {{customer_name}},

We wanted to let you know about an incident affecting {{affected_service}} beginning at {{start_time}} UTC. Short summary: {{one_line_summary}}

What we're doing now: {{mitigation_steps}}
Expected impact: {{affected_customers}}
Next update: We will send another update by {{next_update_time}} or sooner if there is a material change.

If you need immediate assistance, reply to this email or contact support@redwood.ai and reference {{incident_id}}.

Thanks for your patience,
The Redwood Inference team

Maria Gonzalez: Can we add an optional section for customers on Dedicated/Dedicated+Private plans with their account manager contact info? Might reduce support churn.

Kevin O'Neal: yes — add line: "If you are a Dedicated customer, your account manager is {{am_name}} ({{am_email}})."

-- INTERNAL SLACK UPDATE TEMPLATE (for incident channel / exec ops) --
Use short bullets. Always start with quick TL;DR. Example:
Emma Liu: TL;DR: Investigating increased 5xx errors impacting inference RPCs for ~5% of requests; rollback of recent deploy in progress; mitigation being validated.
- Impact: increased errors and latency for some requests; no data loss suspected.
- Owner: oncall @{{oncall_name}}
- Actions in flight: rollback deploy v{{deploy_id}}, scaling up pool X, attaching extra logging.
- ETA/Next check: 15 minutes
- Customer comms: posted status page + queued customer email to affected list
- Follow-ups: postmortem owner: {{postmortem_owner}}

Sasha Kim: Add measured metrics where possible (error %, affected endpoints). Example: "~5% of inference calls returning 5xx; endpoint /v1/embeddings most affected".

-- ON-CALL HANDOFF SNIPPET (when paging someone or handing over) --
Format: one-line summary; what changed in last hour; outstanding tasks; blockers; contact points; severity and customer impact.
Example:
Handing to: @{{next_oncall}}
Summary: rollback in progress to mitigate elevated 5xx; partial recovery observed; ~20 customers still reporting errors.
Last hour: database failover attempted; rollback started; logs added; mitigation validated on 10% traffic.
Outstanding: finish rollback, confirm error rate <0.5%, publish RCA timeline.
Blockers: need DBA to re-run migration check; logs for trace id XYZ missing.
Contact: @{{escalation_engineer}}, pagerduty oncall

Raj Patel: I propose a short 'language guardrail' list we attach to every public message: 
- No blame or conjecture (avoid "due to X" unless validated)
- Use "we are" not "systems are"
- Do not include internal JIRA/PR links in customer-facing text
- Provide a clear follow-up time or say "We will update within X minutes"

Emma Liu: +1. Also let's standardize placeholders naming (use double-curly style like {{incident_id}}).

-- INCIDENT-BOT TEMPLATE (for auto Slack posts) --
```
incident: {{incident_id}}
status: {{status}}
summary: {{one_line_summary}}
owner: @{{oncall_name}}
impact: {{affected_customers}}
link: {{status_page_url}}
```
(incident-bot should expand link to status page and pin the message in the channel)

incident-bot: note: bot already adds created_by and severity fields automatically.

Maria Gonzalez: small ask — can we include an "audience" tag in templates so customer-tiered messaging is easier? e.g., [public], [private:enterprise], [internal]. Then automations can pick the right template.

Kevin O'Neal: good idea. Also recommend a "severity to tone" map: Sev1 = direct, urgent, explicit ETA; Sev2 = factual + next update window; Sev3 = informational. We'll add to README.

Emma Liu: ACTIONS:
- Raj to open PR in docs repo with these text snippets + guardrails (assign: @Raj)
- Maria to add enterprise contact block variants (assign: @Maria)
- Sasha to add example metrics lines and a measurement table snippet (assign: @Sasha)
- Kevin to add severity->tone mapping to the comms README (assign: @Kevin)

Raj Patel: i'll aim to have a PR by EOD today. tagging @PagerDuty and incident-bot owners to ensure automation will pull the right template variables.

Sasha Kim: one more micro-UX note: for the status page, please keep the first update short. Link to a longer incident timeline in the first internal update, not the public gist.

Emma Liu: thanks all. i'll shepherd the PR merge and then we'll do a quick playbook runbook test next oncall shift to validate templates in a real pager scenario. :white_check_mark:

PagerDuty: on-call acknowledgement by Kevin O'Neal at 2026-03-15T14:17:23Z

Kevin O'Neal: acknowledged. i'll be the point for the handoff tonight if needed.

Emma Liu: closing thread for comments; if you want to edit the PR directly please do. will keep the incident channel updated when templates land. :sparkles:
